While it simmers, slice the soaked shiitake and fry it in a dry non-stick pan until browned and a little crisp at the edges. Splash in the tamari and take it off the heat. Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and drain, and toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes.

Stir the ground flax into the congee, then ladle it into bowls. Top with the shiitake, the edamame, the rest of the ginger, the scallion and the almonds, and finish with a pinch of white pepper and the sesame oil.
Cool the second portion and keep it in the fridge. Tomorrow, loosen it with a splash of soy milk or water over low heat.
tip: In a pressure cooker, cook the rice and mung for 35 minutes, then simmer the soy milk in for 10. Start the rice the night before in a slow cooker and breakfast takes 15 minutes.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Edamame and soba salad with sesame-miso dressing
inspiredBy: Japanese cold soba and goma-ae style sesame dressing, with edamame carrying the protein
about: Chewy buckwheat noodles with plenty of edamame and fine napa and carrot in a nutty goma-ae style sesame and miso dressing. It packs well and is fine at room temperature. The **edamame carry the protein**, with buckwheat for extra fibre.
steps: Boil the edamame for 3 to 4 minutes, drain and cool them under cold water.
Cook the soba in plenty of boiling water for the time on the package. Drain, rinse under cold running water, rubbing gently, until the noodles are cold and no longer slippery. Drain well.

Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar or the bottom of a bowl with the back of a spoon until it is a chunky paste. Whisk in the miso, rice vinegar, tamari, sugar, ginger and a splash of water until smooth and pourable.
Shred the napa and carrot finely and slice the scallion.
Toss the noodles, edamame and vegetables with the dressing and scatter over the scallion.
tip: Keep the dressing in a jar and toss it in just before eating if you are packing this for work.

name: Mapo tofu with mushrooms and soy mince, garlicky cauliflower and brown rice
inspiredBy: Sichuan mapo doufu, with mushrooms and soy mince doing the job of the pork, and garlicky stir-fried cauliflower, Sichuan-house style
about: Silky tofu in a brick-red, tingly sauce of fermented chili bean paste, garlic and Sichuan peppercorn, with browned mushrooms and soy mince for a meaty bite. A side of garlicky cauliflower makes it a full plate. The **calcium-set tofu is a big calcium source**.
steps: Cover the soy mince and the dried shiitake with hot water and leave them 10 minutes. Squeeze the mince dry and dice the shiitake. Simmer the tofu cubes in just-boiled water with the salt and a pinch of white pepper for 3 minutes to firm them up, then drain gently.

Heat about two thirds of the canola oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the soy mince, shiitake and oyster mushrooms until they are browned and a bit crispy at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Push them aside, add the doubanjiang and black beans and fry for a minute until the oil turns red and smells rich. Stir in half the garlic and the ginger for 30 seconds.
Pour in the tamari and a mug of water, bring to a simmer and slide in the tofu. Nudge it gently so the cubes stay whole and simmer 5 minutes.

Stir the cornstarch with a splash of cold water, drizzle it in and cook until the sauce turns glossy. Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for a minute, grind them, and scatter over the dish with most of the scallion.

For the cauliflower, heat the last of the oil in a separate pan over high heat and fry the florets for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned in spots. Add the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds, then a splash of water, cover and steam 2 minutes until just tender.
Serve the tofu over the rice with the cauliflower alongside. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: The tingle comes from the Sichuan pepper. Use less if you are new to it, and more doubanjiang if you want more heat.
ingredients: the small mince or granule size
Pixian style if you can find it

name: Lemongrass soya chunk and tofu bún chay with herbs and peanuts
inspiredBy: Vietnamese bún chay, the vegetarian noodle bowl of Buddhist kitchens, with a tamari-based nước chấm in place of fish sauce
about: Cool rice vermicelli with lemongrass-seared soya chunks, golden tofu and mushrooms, mint, quick-pickled carrot, crisp napa and crushed peanuts, under a sweet-sour tamari nước chấm. It's cool, herby and packs well for tomorrow. The **soya chunks and tofu bring plenty of protein**.
steps: Cover the soya chunks with hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze them dry and tear them into bite-size pieces. Toss them with the torn mushrooms, the lemongrass, half the garlic, a little of the tamari and a pinch of the sugar. Leave to marinate while you do the rest.
Make the sauce by stirring the rest of the tamari, garlic and sugar with the chili, most of the rice vinegar and a few spoonfuls of water until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the carrot with a little rice vinegar, a pinch of sugar and the salt and leave it to pickle for 10 minutes.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for the time on the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain again.

Heat half the canola oil in a hot non-stick pan and sear the tofu for about 6 minutes, turning, until golden on every side. Lift it out. Add the rest of the oil and sear the soya chunks and mushrooms in two batches, about 4 minutes each, so they brown instead of steaming.
Build the bowls with the shredded napa, noodles, pickled carrot and the seared tofu, soya and mushrooms. Add the mint and peanuts and spoon the sauce over.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow, with the sauce, herbs and noodles kept in separate containers.
tip: Thai basil or perilla, if the grocer has them, is lovely in place of the mint. At the lighter size the noodle nest is small, so pile on the napa, carrot and herbs. The sauce keeps in a jar for up to 4 days.

name: Soft tofu stew (sundubu jjigae) with vegan kimchi and mushrooms
inspiredBy: Korean sundubu jjigae, with a shiitake broth and kimchi in place of the seafood
about: A bubbling, red, chili-spiked stew of soft tofu, kimchi, bok choy and soybean sprouts, finished with ground toasted sesame. It's warming, fast and savoury. The **tofu and sprouts carry the protein**.
steps: Soak the dried shiitake in about two and a half cups of hot water for 15 minutes, then lift them out, slice them and keep the soaking water as your stock.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for a minute and grind them to a rough powder. Cut the bok choy into chunks.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the garlic, kimchi and gochugaru and stir for 2 minutes until the kimchi smells toasty.
Pour in the shiitake stock and simmer the kimchi, shiitake, sprouts, frozen edamame and bok choy for 8 minutes.
Spoon in the soft tofu in big chunks, season with the tamari and simmer 4 minutes more, without stirring too much so the tofu stays in clouds.
Stir in the ground sesame and the scallion, and serve bubbling hot with the rice. Cool the second portion for tomorrow's lunch and reheat gently.
tip: Most jarred kimchi is made with fish sauce or salted shrimp. Look for one labelled vegan, or leave it out and add a splash more tamari and a pinch of chili. If the tofu breaks up when you reheat it, that's the style. Medium-firm tofu also works, but it is less custardy.
ingredients: 1 tube of soft (silken) tofu, calcium-set if you can find it
vegan, with no fish sauce or shrimp (check the label)
stems and leaves, cut into chunks

name: Tempeh and broccoli stir-fry with black bean sauce and brown rice
inspiredBy: Cantonese broccoli in black bean sauce, usually made with beef, here with tempeh
about: Golden pan-fried tempeh with broccoli and cauliflower in a glossy, garlicky sauce of fermented black beans and ginger. It comes together in one pan in about 30 minutes. The **tempeh brings about 22 g of protein**, and the broccoli covers vitamin C.
steps: Simmer the tempeh in a pan of water for 5 minutes to soften it and mellow its flavour. Drain, pat dry and cut it into thin slabs.
Heat half the canola oil in a wok or large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry the tempeh until golden on both sides, about 6 minutes. Lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic, ginger, black beans and chili, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the cauliflower, carrot and a splash of water, cover and steam for 2 minutes, then add the broccoli, cover again and steam 3 minutes more, until the cauliflower is tender and the broccoli is bright green.
Stir the tamari, sugar and cornstarch with a few spoonfuls of cold water and stir it in at the end. Cook until glossy, then return the tempeh to the pan and toss to coat.
Finish with the scallion and serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Rinse the black beans so the dish isn't too salty. They are the whole flavour of the sauce, so don't skip them.
ingredients: cut into small florets, stems peeled and sliced

name: Seitan teriyaki with edamame, simmered sweet potato and bok choy
inspiredBy: Japanese teriyaki with satsuma-imo no nimono (simmered sweet potato), with seitan as the protein
about: Seared seitan and oyster mushrooms in a glossy ginger-teriyaki glaze, with soft simmered sweet potato, edamame and bok choy on brown rice. It's sticky, sweet and savoury in all the right places. The **seitan and edamame** together bring over 30 g of protein.
steps: Put the sweet potato in a pot with a cup of water, a third of the sugar and a splash of the tamari. Simmer, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then uncover and let the liquid cook down to a glaze.
Mix the rest of the tamari and sugar with the ginger and a splash of water to make the teriyaki sauce.

Slice the seitan into thick pieces and tear the mushrooms into strips. Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the seitan and mushrooms for 5 to 6 minutes, until browned on the edges.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble and thicken for 2 minutes, turning the seitan so it is coated and glossy.
Drop the frozen edamame and the bok choy into the sweet potato pot for the last 3 minutes of cooking, until the edamame is hot and the bok choy is bright and just tender.
Serve the seitan over the rice with the sweet potato, edamame and bok choy, and scatter over the sesame seeds and scallion. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Buy plain seitan, not the flavoured kinds, so the teriyaki can do the flavouring. Pan-seared firm tofu works in place of seitan if you don't want the gluten.

name: Vegan bibimbap with crispy tofu, tempeh bulgogi and four namul
inspiredBy: Korean bibimbap, with pan-crisped tofu and bulgogi-style tempeh in place of the beef and egg
about: A big bowl of brown rice topped with crisp-edged tofu, savoury tempeh bulgogi and colourful sautéed vegetables, with a spoonful of gochujang sauce to stir through. It's a weekend project that makes two bowls. The **tofu and tempeh bring plenty of protein**, with calcium from the tofu.
steps: Soak the dried shiitake in hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze it dry and slice it. Crumble the tempeh into small pieces and toss it with half the tamari, the sugar, half the sesame oil and a little of the garlic. Leave it to marinate.

Boil the soybean sprouts in a covered pot with a splash of water for 5 minutes, drain and toss with a little garlic, a few drops of the sesame oil and a pinch of the salt. Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, squeeze it dry and season it the same way.

Heat a little of the canola oil in a non-stick pan and, one vegetable at a time, sauté the carrot, then the shiitake, each for 2 to 3 minutes with a pinch of salt and a little garlic. Keep each pile separate on a big plate.
Brown the tofu slices in some of the remaining oil for about 3 minutes a side until crisp at the edges. Then sear the marinated tempeh in the same pan until sticky and browned, about 4 minutes.
Make the sauce by stirring the gochujang with the rest of the sesame oil and tamari, a spoonful of water and most of the sesame seeds. The gochujang is for the sauce, not the marinade.
Warm the rice and divide it between two bowls. Arrange the tofu, the tempeh bulgogi and the namul in neat piles on top, scatter over the rest of the sesame seeds, and add the sauce.
Mix everything together at the table. Keep the second portion's toppings and rice in separate containers for tomorrow.
tip: Tomorrow, re-crisp the tofu in a hot pan for 2 minutes and eat the rest at room temperature, like a dosirak lunchbox. For the crispy rice base you get at restaurants, press the rice into an oiled hot skillet for a couple of minutes before piling the toppings on.

name: Soy milk hot pot (tonyu nabe) with tofu, edamame and napa cabbage
inspiredBy: Japanese tonyu nabe, the creamy soy milk hot pot, with a goma dare (sesame) dip
about: A pot of gently simmering, creamy soy milk broth with tofu, edamame, napa cabbage, carrot and shiitake, and a nutty sesame dipping sauce. It's an easy, relaxed Sunday supper. The **soy milk and tofu bring protein and calcium**.
steps: Soak the dried shiitake in a cup of hot water for 15 minutes. Soak the vermicelli in warm water for 5 minutes and drain it. Chop the napa, separating the white stems from the leaves.
For the dipping sauce (goma dare), stir the tamari, rice vinegar, ground sesame paste and half the scallion with a spoonful of hot water, until it is thick and nutty.
Slice the soaked shiitake. Pour the shiitake soaking water and an equal amount of fresh water into a wide pot, add the ginger and carrot, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the napa stems and simmer 5 minutes, then turn the heat to low and pour in the soy milk. Keep it at a gentle simmer, never a hard boil, or it will split.

Whisk the miso with a ladleful of the broth and stir it back in. Add the tofu, frozen edamame, shiitake and napa leaves and cook for 5 minutes, until everything is hot through. Stir in the noodles for the last 2 minutes.
Serve straight from the pot with the dipping sauce and the rest of the scallion.
tip: End the pot the Japanese way: skip the noodles, stir a scoop of leftover brown rice into the last of the broth and simmer it for a few minutes as zosui. Double it for company and set the pot in the middle of the table.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)
toasted and ground to a paste

name: Warm black sesame and almond soy milk
inspiredBy: Chinese black sesame and almond paste (zhi ma xing ren hu) and Japanese kuro goma kinako milk, loosened with soy milk and thickened with a little ground flax
about: A nutty, toasty drink of blended black sesame, almonds and kinako, warmed with fortified soy milk and thickened with a little ground flax, like a thin hu. It feels like a treat and takes five minutes. It brings **B12, calcium, vitamin E and plant omega-3** in one cup.
steps: Toast the black sesame and almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they smell nutty.
Blend them with the kinako, ground flax, sugar and the cold soy milk until completely smooth, about a minute.
Pour into a small pot and warm gently for a couple of minutes, stirring the bottom, until steaming. Don't boil it, or the flax turns gluey.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Warm kinako soy latte
inspiredBy: Japanese kinako (roasted soybean flour) milk, with almonds
about: A toasty, nutty mug of kinako (roasted soybean flour) and ground almonds whisked into warm fortified soy milk, with a little ground flax for body. It tastes like the best part of a peanut butter cookie. It brings **B12, calcium, vitamin E and plant protein**.
steps: Grind the almonds to a fine powder in a blender or spice grinder.
Whisk the kinako, ground almonds, ground flax and sugar into a splash of the cold soy milk until it makes a smooth paste.
Warm the rest of the soy milk until steaming, whisk in the paste and heat for a minute more, stirring. Pour into a mug and drink warm.
tip: Look for kinako at a Japanese grocer, or konggaru (Korean roasted soybean powder) at H Mart or T&T. They are the same thing. At a pinch, grind roasted soy nuts as fine as you can.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)
ground fine in a blender or mortar

name: Warm ginger soy milk with almonds
inspiredBy: Japanese shoga tonyu (hot ginger soy milk), blended with almonds
about: A cosy cup of ginger soy milk blended with almonds, sweet but not too sweet and gently warming. It takes five minutes. It brings **B12, calcium and vitamin E** in one mug.
steps: Blend the almonds, ground flax and sugar with about a third of the cold soy milk until smooth, about a minute.
Simmer the ginger slices in the rest of the soy milk for 3 minutes, gently, without boiling hard. Lift out the ginger.
Whisk in the almond mix and warm for a minute more, stirring, until steaming. Pour into a mug and drink warm.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Warm sweet potato soy latte (goguma latte)
inspiredBy: the Korean cafe goguma latte, made with soy milk and almonds, with a spoonful of konggaru (roasted soybean powder) for an injeolmi note
about: A creamy, naturally sweet Korean cafe drink of blended sweet potato, almonds, a spoonful of roasted soybean powder (kinako or konggaru) and soy milk, with a dusting of cinnamon. The sweet potato makes it taste like dessert. It brings **B12, calcium and vitamin A**.
steps: Roast or steam the sweet potato until very soft (or use one from the fridge) and peel it. Blend it with the almonds, kinako, flax, the cold soy milk, ginger and cinnamon until completely smooth.
Warm in a small pot for 3 minutes, stirring the bottom, until steaming. Drink it warm.
tip: Roast or steam a few sweet potatoes at once and keep them in the fridge for 4 days.
ingredients: unsweetened, fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)
roasted or steamed until very soft, skin removed

name: Roasted soybeans with a mandarin
inspiredBy: Japanese irimame (roasted soybeans), eaten with winter citrus
about: A handful of crunchy roasted soybeans and a juicy mandarin. It's a quick, no-cook snack. The **soybeans bring about 13 g of protein**, and the mandarin brings vitamin C.
steps: Tip the roasted soybeans into a small bowl.
Peel the mandarin and eat it alongside, a segment between handfuls.
tip: Look for them as soy nuts in the bulk or snack aisle. Unsalted is best.

name: Warm chili-garlic edamame with a mandarin
inspiredBy: Japanese edamame with salt, with a Korean-style chili and garlic kick
about: Warm, salty edamame tossed with garlic, a little tamari and chili, with a mandarin on the side. It takes about five minutes. The **edamame bring protein, fibre and folate**, and the mandarin adds vitamin C.
steps: Boil the edamame for 3 to 4 minutes and drain well.
Toss with the garlic, tamari and chili while still warm, then eat them right away with the mandarin.

name: Chilled tofu (hiyayakko) with ginger, scallion and tamari
inspiredBy: Japanese hiyayakko, the simplest cold tofu plate
about: A block of cool tofu with grated ginger, scallion, toasted sesame and a splash of tamari. It's the simplest Japanese cold plate and takes two minutes. The **tofu brings calcium and protein** in a clean, fresh snack.
steps: Drain the tofu, pat it dry and cut it into big squares on a small plate.
Top with the ginger, scallion and sesame and spoon the tamari over just before eating.

name: Warm salted edamame
inspiredBy: Japanese edamame with sea salt, the classic izakaya snack
about: A bowl of warm, lightly salted edamame, the classic izakaya snack. They take five minutes. The **edamame bring protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Boil the edamame for 3 to 4 minutes and drain well.
Toss with a pinch of salt and eat them warm.

name: Soy-glazed toasted almonds
inspiredBy: Japanese and Korean tamari-glazed nuts
about: Almonds toasted in a dry pan and glazed with a splash of tamari and a pinch of sugar until they're dark, salty and a bit sticky. A small handful is plenty. The **almonds are rich in vitamin E**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, shaking often, until they smell nutty.
Stir the tamari and sugar with a spoonful of water, pour it into the pan and stir for about a minute, until the glaze has cooked on and the pan is dry.
Tip onto a plate to cool and crisp up.

name: Sweet mung bean soup (lu dou sha)
inspiredBy: Cantonese lu dou sha, the smooth sweet soup of hulled mung beans
about: A soft, lightly sweet soup of split mung beans simmered with a little ginger. It's lovely warm or chilled. The **mung beans bring plant protein and folate**.
steps: Rinse the mung beans and put them in a small pot with about five times their volume of water and the ginger.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for about 20 minutes, until the beans have broken down into a thick, soft soup.
Stir in the sugar, simmer 2 minutes more, and serve warm or chilled.
tip: It makes two bowls. Keep the second in the fridge for up to 4 days and eat it warm or chilled.

name: Chilled tofu and edamame plate with sesame and ginger
inspiredBy: a Japanese izakaya cold plate of tofu and edamame
about: Soft cool tofu and warm edamame with grated ginger, toasted black sesame and a splash of tamari. It takes five minutes. It's a **protein-rich snack with calcium and folate**.
steps: Boil the edamame for 3 to 4 minutes, drain and let them cool a little.
Cut the tofu into squares on a small plate, add the ginger, sesame and the warm edamame, and spoon the tamari over.

name: Moong and besan chilla with spinach and mint chutney
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Gujarati besan chilla, with moong dal for more protein
about: Savoury lentil pancakes with spinach, onion and tomato, crisp at the edges and soft in the middle, with a sharp mint and green chili chutney. The **moong dal and besan together** bring about 20 g of protein, and the ground flax in the chutney adds plant omega-3 you won't taste.
steps: The night before, rinse the moong dal and soak it in plenty of water for at least 4 hours or overnight (Sunday night for Monday).

Drain the dal and blend it with the besan, a squeeze of the lemon juice and enough water to make a thick, pourable batter, like pancake batter. Stir in the onion, tomato, spinach, half the green chili, half the cilantro, turmeric, chili powder, ajwain, cumin and salt.
For the chutney, blitz the mint, the rest of the cilantro, the rest of the green chili, the rest of the lemon juice and the ground flax with a splash of water until smooth.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and brush it with a little of the oil. Pour in a ladleful of batter and spread it thin and round. Cook until the underside is golden and the edges lift, about 3 minutes.
Brush a touch of oil on top, flip, and cook 2 minutes more until speckled brown. Repeat with the rest of the batter, keeping the finished chillas warm under a plate.
Stack the chillas and serve with the chutney for dunking.
tip: Blend the dal and besan the night before and stir in the chopped vegetables in the morning, and breakfast takes 15 minutes. The plain batter keeps 2 days in the fridge and the chutney keeps 3.

name: Kanda poha with peanuts and peas, and a cup of soy masala chai
inspiredBy: Maharashtrian kanda poha with the classic chai alongside, soy beverage in place of milk
about: Fluffy flattened rice tossed with onion, turmeric, curry leaves, crunchy peanuts and sweet peas, finished with lemon and cilantro, with a cup of ginger-cardamom chai alongside. The chai is made with fortified soy beverage, so this breakfast quietly brings your **vitamin B12 and calcium**, and the peanuts bring protein and vitamin E.
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander under cool running water for a few seconds, just until the flakes soften but still hold their shape, and leave it to drain. It keeps softening as it sits.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the peanuts until golden and crunchy, about 2 minutes. Scoop them out and set aside.
In the same oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and green chili. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric and peas with a splash of water and cook 3 minutes, until the peas are tender.

Add the poha, the rest of the salt and a pinch of jaggery and toss gently so the flakes don't break. Cover and steam on low heat for 2 minutes, then turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, cilantro and peanuts.

For the chai, steep the tea bags in 70 ml of just-boiled water for 4 minutes. Meanwhile, warm the soy beverage with the ginger, cardamom and the rest of the jaggery over gentle heat until it steams, without letting it boil hard. Off the heat, pour in the hot tea and strain into a mug.
tip: Chop the onion and slit the chilies the night before and breakfast is on the table in 15 minutes.
ingredients: thick poha (jada poha), dry, from any Indian grocer
fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)
2 tea bags (or 2 tsp loose Assam or CTC) steeped in 70 ml hot water
a pinch goes in the poha, the rest in the chai

name: Idli with sambar and flax-peanut chutney powder
inspiredBy: Tamil and Karnataka tiffin: idli, sambar and idli podi
about: Soft steamed rice-and-urad idlis with a tangy, vegetable-packed sambar and a spoonful of oily, nutty chutney powder. It is a weekend project that makes two mornings, and the **toor, urad and flax together** bring protein, iron and plant omega-3 in a breakfast that tastes like a Chennai tiffin stop.
steps: Friday afternoon, soak the rice and the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds separately in plenty of water for at least 5 hours.

Drain and grind the urad until fluffy and thick, then the rice until slightly grainy. Mix both with half the salt, by hand, cover loosely and leave in a warm spot for 8 to 10 hours, until the batter has risen and smells pleasantly sour.
Saturday morning, pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and a little water until completely soft, about 20 minutes, and mash it.
Simmer the carrot, onion and tomato in water with the tamarind, sambar powder and salt until tender, about 12 minutes. Stir in the mashed dal and simmer 8 minutes more.
Heat half the oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and hing. Pour the tempering into the sambar and add the cilantro.
Grease an idli steamer, fill the moulds with batter and steam for 12 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

For the chutney powder, dry-toast the flax, peanuts, sesame and a few curry leaves until fragrant and crisp, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the chili powder. Grind coarsely with a pinch of salt and stir in the rest of the oil to make a crumbly paste.
Serve a few idlis with the sambar and a spoonful of chutney powder on the side. Keep the rest of the idlis, sambar and powder for Sunday, and re-steam the idlis for 3 minutes to soften them.
tip: Idli batter grinds and ferments best in a bigger batch. Soak about ¾ cup of idli rice and ½ cup of urad dal (with ¼ tsp fenugreek seeds), steam the idlis this plan needs, and keep the rest of the batter in the fridge for up to 4 days for dosas, or freeze spare idlis. Cool kitchen? Set the batter in the oven with only the light on. The chutney powder keeps 2 weeks in a jar.
ingredients: idli rice or any parboiled rice, dry

name: Tofu and mushroom tikka chana chaat bowl with tamarind and soy yogurt
inspiredBy: Delhi chaat and paneer or mushroom tikka chaat, with calcium-set tofu in place of the paneer
about: Charred, tandoori-spiced tofu and mushrooms over a tangy chaat of chickpeas, sweet potato, cucumber and tomato, finished with tamarind, lemon and a cooling soy-yogurt drizzle. It is a proper lunch with **about 30 g of protein**, and the tomato and lemon help you absorb the iron from the chickpeas.
steps: Pat the tofu dry and toss the cubes and the mushrooms with a third of the soy yogurt, the Kashmiri chili, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Leave to marinate while you do the rest, at least 15 minutes.
Boil the sweet potato in salted water until just tender, about 8 minutes, then drain and let it cool a little.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu and mushrooms, turning gently now and then, until golden and a little charred at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Loosen the tamarind and jaggery with a spoonful of warm water to make a quick sweet-sour chutney.
In a bowl, toss the chickpeas, sweet potato, cucumber, tomato, onion and cilantro with the tamarind, the rest of the lemon juice, chaat masala and kala namak.
Pile the chaat in a bowl, top with the hot tofu and mushrooms, and spoon over the rest of the soy yogurt.
tip: Boil the sweet potato and marinate the tofu and mushrooms the night before. At lunch, sear them for 8 minutes while you toss the chaat.
ingredients: firm, set with calcium sulfate (check the label), cubed
oyster or white button mushrooms, halved
a third marinates the tofu and mushrooms, the rest goes on top

name: Rajma masala with brown basmati and cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Punjabi rajma chawal, finished with almond instead of cream
about: Kidney beans simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala until the gravy clings, with brown basmati and a cooling soy-yogurt raita. Rajma is a **great iron source**, and the tomato in the masala brings vitamin C that helps you absorb it. It is even better tomorrow, so lunch is made.
steps: The night before, soak the rajma in plenty of cold water.

Drain the beans and pressure-cook them with fresh water, the bay leaf and a pinch of salt until completely soft and easy to crush, about 25 minutes. Without a pressure cooker, simmer them covered for about an hour, topping up the water.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wide pot, sizzle the cumin, then add the onion and cook until deep golden, about 10 minutes. Add the ginger, garlic and green chili for the last 2 minutes.

Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and a pinch of salt. Cook until the tomatoes collapse and the oil starts to separate at the edges, about 8 minutes, then stir in the almond paste.

Add the beans with their cooking water and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few against the side of the pot, until the gravy is thick. Stir in the garam masala and the kasuri methi, crushed between your palms.
Cook the brown basmati in plenty of salted boiling water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.
For the raita, squeeze the grated cucumber dry and stir it into the soy yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Serve the rajma over the rice with the raita and a handful of cilantro. Pack the second portion, with its own rice and raita, for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: No time to soak? Use two cans of kidney beans, drained, and simmer them in the masala for 20 minutes. At a lighter size, the rice is a small scoop, about a quarter cup cooked.
ingredients: blanched or soaked, blended into a paste with a little water

name: Palak tofu with whole-wheat roti
inspiredBy: Punjabi palak paneer, with calcium-set tofu in place of paneer
about: Cubes of golden pan-seared tofu in a silky spinach gravy with ginger, garlic and a little almond for richness, scooped up with soft whole-wheat roti. The **calcium-set tofu brings plenty of calcium**, and the spinach brings folate and vitamin K. Tomorrow's lunch is cooked too.
steps: Blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling water for 1 minute, then plunge it into cold water so it stays bright green. Squeeze it dry and blend it smooth with the green chili and a splash of water.
Pat the tofu dry and sear it in half the oil in a non-stick pan until golden on a couple of sides, about 6 minutes. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and set aside.
In a wide pot, heat the rest of the oil and sizzle the cumin. Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes, adding the ginger and garlic for the last 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt. Cook until jammy, about 6 minutes, then stir in the almond paste.

Pour in the spinach purée and simmer gently for 5 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick. Stir in the garam masala and the kasuri methi, crushed between your palms, then slide in the tofu and warm it through for 3 minutes.

For the rotis, mix the atta with warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest it 10 minutes. Roll thin rounds and cook them on a hot dry pan until they puff and show brown spots. Make a few extra for tomorrow.
Serve the palak tofu with the hot rotis. Pack the second portion and its rotis for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Pressed for time? Use a pack of frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry, and skip the blanching. At a lighter size, one small, palm-sized roti is the right amount.
ingredients: firm, set with calcium sulfate (check the label), cubed
blanched or soaked, blended into a paste with a little water

name: Gujarati soy-yogurt kadhi with moong khichdi and cauliflower-carrot shaak
inspiredBy: Gujarati kadhi khichdi, with soy yogurt standing in for the dahi
about: A comforting plate of soft moong dal and rice khichdi, a tangy-sweet besan kadhi tempered with curry leaves, and a quick mustard-seed stir-fry of cauliflower and carrot. The moong, besan and soy yogurt together give you **about 35 g of protein**, and it tastes even better the second day.
steps: Rinse the moong dal and rice together and cook with half the turmeric, a pinch of salt and about 3 cups of water, covered, until very soft and porridge-like, about 40 minutes.
For the kadhi, whisk the besan into the soy yogurt until completely smooth, then loosen with water to the thickness of thin cream. Add the ginger, jaggery, a pinch of the turmeric and salt.

Warm the kadhi over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens, then keep it at a gentle bubble for 10 minutes. A hard boil can split soy yogurt, so keep the heat low. If your soy yogurt is mild, finish with a teaspoon of lemon juice.
Heat half the oil in a small pan, crackle the cumin seeds, then add the curry leaves, green chili, hing and Kashmiri chili. Pour this tempering over the kadhi and stir in half the cilantro.

For the shaak, heat the rest of the oil in a wide pan and crackle the mustard seeds. Add the cauliflower, carrot and peas with the rest of the turmeric and a pinch of salt, and stir-fry over medium-high heat with a splash of water for 7 minutes, until just tender with a little char.

Serve the khichdi in bowls with the kadhi poured over and the shaak on the side, topped with the rest of the cilantro. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch and loosen the kadhi with a splash of water when you reheat it.
tip: Short on time? Pressure-cook the khichdi for 15 minutes.

name: Soya, moong and mushroom keema matar with whole-wheat roti
inspiredBy: Mumbai and Punjabi keema matar, with soy granules in place of the mince
about: A dry, richly spiced mince-style curry of soy granules, a little split moong dal and chopped mushrooms with sweet peas, ginger and garam masala, with a squeeze of lemon and a warm roti. The granules and moong bring **about 35 g of protein**, and the peas and tomato add vitamin C. It reheats well for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Rinse the moong dal and soak it in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain. Soak the soy granules in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze them dry.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and sizzle the cumin. Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes, adding the ginger, garlic and green chili for the last 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt, and cook until the tomatoes break down into a thick paste, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the soy granules and moong dal with half a cup of water. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the dal is tender and the pan is nearly dry.
Add the peas and mushrooms and cook 6 minutes more, until the mushrooms have given up their water and the pan is dry again, then finish with the garam masala, amchur and cilantro.
For the rotis, mix the atta with warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough, rest 10 minutes, then roll and cook on a hot dry pan until puffed and speckled. Make extras for tomorrow.
Serve the keema hot with the rotis and a squeeze of lemon. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Soy granules are sold as soya granules or textured vegetable protein, usually in the Indian or natural-foods aisle. At a lighter size, make one small, palm-sized roti.
ingredients: dry soy granules, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes and squeezed dry
oyster or white button mushrooms, finely chopped

name: Kerala-style tofu roast with carrot and cabbage thoran and brown rice
inspiredBy: Kerala nadan roasts, usually made with beef or prawns, here with calcium-set tofu
about: Seared tofu coated in a dark, peppery onion-tomato roast with crisp coconut slivers and curry leaves, with a quick carrot and cabbage thoran and brown rice. The **calcium-set tofu is the protein and calcium**, and the lemon at the end helps your body absorb the iron in the tofu and rice.
steps: Cook the brown basmati in plenty of salted boiling water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.
Pat the tofu dry and toss with the turmeric, half the pepper and a pinch of salt. Sear it in a little of the oil in a non-stick pan until golden, about 6 minutes, and set aside.

In a wide pan, fry the coconut slivers in a little oil until golden and nutty-smelling, about 2 minutes, and scoop them out. In the same oil, cook the onion with half the curry leaves until deep brown, about 12 minutes, adding the garlic, ginger and green chili for the last 2 minutes.
Stir in the Kashmiri chili, ground coriander, fennel, garam masala and the rest of the pepper for 30 seconds, then add the tomato and a splash of water. Simmer until jammy, about 8 minutes.
Fold the tofu and the fried coconut back into the masala and cook 5 minutes, until the masala clings and turns glossy. Squeeze over the lemon juice.

For the thoran, heat a little oil in a pan and crackle the mustard seeds with the rest of the curry leaves. Add the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the turmeric and a pinch of salt, cover and cook 4 minutes, then stir in the grated coconut and cook uncovered for 2 minutes.
Serve the roast with the rice and thoran. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Short on time? Make the masala on Thursday night and finish with the tofu on Friday, and fry frozen grated coconut for 1 minute in place of fresh slivers. At a lighter size, the rice is a small scoop, about a third of a cup cooked.
ingredients: firm, set with calcium sulfate (check the label), cubed
fresh or frozen; half in slivers for the roast, half grated for the thoran

name: Soya chunk and mushroom dum biryani with mint raita
inspiredBy: Hyderabadi dum biryani, with soya chunks marinated in soy yogurt
about: A weekend project that earns its keep: soya chunks marinated in spiced soy yogurt, layered with half-cooked brown basmati, fried onions, peas, mushrooms, mint and saffron soy beverage, then sealed and steamed so every grain picks up the flavour. The chunks and yogurt bring **most of the protein**, about 45 g on the plate, and there is a portion for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Fry the sliced onion in half the oil over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden and crisp at the edges, about 15 minutes. Scoop it out onto paper towels. Fry the slivered almonds in the same oil until pale gold, and set both aside.

Boil the soya chunks in salted water for 8 minutes, drain and squeeze them dry. Toss them with most of the soy yogurt, the ginger, garlic, green chili, garam masala, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, salt and half the fried onions. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Warm the soy beverage and steep the saffron in it.

Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of salted water with the bay leaf, cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, clove and cumin until about three-quarters cooked, 20 minutes or so. It should still have a firm core. Drain.
In a heavy pot, warm the rest of the oil and cook the marinated chunks with the peas and mushrooms for 6 minutes, until the marinade thickens.
Spread the rice over the marinated chunks. Scatter most of the mint and the rest of the fried onions on top, then drizzle with the saffron soy beverage.
Cover the pot with foil and a tight lid. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Stir the remaining soy yogurt with the rest of the chopped mint and a pinch of salt for the raita.
Fluff the biryani gently from the bottom up, top with the almonds and serve with the raita. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Marinate the soya chunks on Friday night and the whole dish moves faster on Saturday.
ingredients: oyster or white button mushrooms, halved
plain; most for the marinade, the rest for the raita

name: Dal tadka with whole-wheat roti and gobi matar
inspiredBy: North Indian dal tadka and dal palak, with a dhaba-style cauliflower, pea and mushroom sabzi
about: Toor and moong dal with a handful of spinach, simmered soft and finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tadka, with a dry cauliflower, pea and mushroom sabzi sharpened with amchur and a warm whole-wheat roti. The dals and spinach bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the cauliflower adds vitamin C and choline. It is Sunday-evening home cooking.
steps: Rinse the toor and moong dal and cook them with half the turmeric, half the tomato, half the ginger, a pinch of salt and plenty of water until completely soft, about 20 minutes in a pressure cooker or 45 in a covered pot. Whisk until creamy, then stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 2 minutes.

For the sabzi, heat a little of the oil in a pan, sizzle a pinch of the cumin, then add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the cauliflower, peas, mushrooms, the rest of the ginger, a little turmeric and Kashmiri chili, the ground coriander, amchur and salt with a splash of water, cover and cook until tender but not mushy, about 10 minutes.
For the rotis, mix the atta with warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest it 10 minutes. Roll thin rounds and cook them on a hot dry pan until they puff and show brown spots.

For the tadka, heat the rest of the oil until shimmering, sizzle the cumin, garlic and green chili until the garlic is golden, then add the hing, the rest of the Kashmiri chili and the rest of the tomato for a minute. Pour it over the dal.
Squeeze lemon over the dal and serve it with the rotis and the cauliflower, pea and mushroom sabzi.
tip: At a lighter size, make one small, palm-sized roti.
ingredients: oyster or white button mushrooms, sliced

name: Soy masala chai
inspiredBy: everyday masala chai, made with soy beverage
about: A strong ginger-cardamom tea made with fortified soy beverage and a little jaggery. It is the easiest way to get your **vitamin B12 and calcium** in a day, and it still tastes like proper chai.
steps: Steep the tea bags in 70 ml of just-boiled water for 4 minutes, then squeeze and remove them.
Warm the soy beverage with the ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and jaggery over gentle heat for 4 minutes, until it steams. Don't let it boil hard.
Off the heat, pour in the hot tea and strain into a big mug. Adding the tea last keeps the soy beverage from curdling.
tip: Check your carton for B12: this plan counts on about 2 µg per cup. Many Canadian cartons carry about half that, so a B12 supplement is the safe bet.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)
2 tea bags (or 2 tsp loose Assam or CTC) steeped in 70 ml hot water

name: Masala roasted chana
inspiredBy: the roasted chana sold by street vendors all over India, made at home from canned chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with chaat masala, chili and lemon. A crunchy, protein-rich snack, best eaten the day you roast it.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Toss the very dry chickpeas with the oil, cumin, Kashmiri chili and salt.
Spread on a tray and roast, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crunchy, about 30 minutes.
Toss with the chaat masala and lemon juice while still hot. Eat the same day for the best crunch.
ingredients: canned, drained, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Peanut sundal
inspiredBy: Tamil sundal, the beach-snack way
about: Boiled peanuts tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves and fresh coconut, a beachside snack from Chennai. It is filling and rich in **protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Boil the peanuts in salted water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain well.
Heat the oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves, green chili and hing for 30 seconds.
Toss in the peanuts and the coconut and stir for a minute. Serve warm.
tip: Boil a big batch of peanuts on Sunday and keep them in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Guava and mango fruit chaat with walnuts
inspiredBy: Delhi fruit chaat, with walnuts for crunch
about: Crisp guava and sweet mango tossed with lemon, chaat masala and black salt, topped with toasted walnuts for crunch. It is sweet, sour and salty all at once, and guava is a **vitamin C powerhouse**.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until you can smell them, then chop.
Toss the guava and mango with the lemon juice, chaat masala and kala namak.
Top with the warm walnuts and serve right away.
tip: No guava? A crisp pear and two kiwis make a good chaat too.

name: Haldi doodh with almond
inspiredBy: everyday haldi doodh, made with soy beverage and almonds instead of dairy
about: Golden milk made with fortified soy beverage, turmeric, ginger and black pepper, blended with a few almonds for a creamy finish and sweetened with a little jaggery. A cosy evening drink with **vitamin B12 and calcium**.
steps: Blend the almonds and a splash of the soy beverage until smooth.
Warm the rest of the soy beverage with the jaggery, turmeric, ginger, black pepper and cardamom over gentle heat, whisking, for 4 minutes.
Whisk in the almond cream and pour into a mug.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Moong kosambari
inspiredBy: Karnataka kosambari, the temple-festival salad
about: A fresh Karnataka salad of soaked moong dal with cucumber, coconut and lemon, tempered with mustard and curry leaves. It is light, crunchy and cooling, with a surprising amount of **protein, folate and crunch**.
steps: Drain the soaked moong dal. It should be tender but still a little crunchy. Dry-roast the peanuts until golden and crush them coarsely.
Toss the dal with the cucumber, coconut, cilantro, green chili, lemon juice, salt and the crushed roasted peanuts.
Heat the oil, crackle the mustard seeds with the curry leaves, then pour over the salad and mix.
ingredients: dry, split and skinned, soaked 2 hours

name: Til-alsi laddoo with walnuts
inspiredBy: the North Indian winter til-alsi laddoo, bound with jaggery
about: Toasted sesame, flax and walnuts bound with a little melted jaggery into two small laddoos, in the style of the North Indian winter til-alsi laddoo. The sesame brings **calcium and iron**, and the flax and walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Dry-toast the sesame seeds until they turn pale gold and start to pop, about 2 minutes. Tip them out to cool.
Toast the ground flax for 1 minute, and chop the walnuts finely. Melt the jaggery with a spoonful of water in a small pan over low heat until it bubbles into a thick syrup, about 3 minutes.
Stir the sesame, flax, walnuts and cardamom into the syrup, let it cool for a minute until you can handle it, then roll into two small laddoos with damp hands.
tip: Roll a week's worth on Sunday. They keep 10 days in a jar in the fridge.

name: Mango soy lassi with almonds
inspiredBy: Punjabi sweet lassi, with almonds, soy yogurt and soy beverage
about: A cold, frothy lassi of soy yogurt, fortified soy beverage, sweet mango and blended almonds, with a pinch of cardamom. It is creamy and quietly brings your **vitamin B12 and calcium**, plus vitamin C from the mango.
steps: Blend the soy beverage, soy yogurt, mango, almonds and cardamom until smooth and frothy.
Pour over ice if you like and drink right away.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Cucumber and peanut koshimbir
inspiredBy: Maharashtrian kakdi koshimbir
about: A cool Maharashtrian salad of cucumber with coarsely ground roasted peanuts, lemon and green chili. It is crunchy, fresh and gently sweet-sour, with **protein and healthy fats** from the peanuts.
steps: Dry-roast the peanuts in a pan until golden and fragrant, about 4 minutes, adding the cumin seeds for the last minute, then crush them coarsely together.
Toss the cucumber with the green chili, lemon juice, jaggery and salt.
Stir in most of the peanuts and cilantro just before serving, then top with the rest.

name: Brown rice kheer with soy beverage and almonds
inspiredBy: Bengali and North Indian rice kheer, with soy beverage
about: Creamy rice pudding simmered in fortified soy beverage with cardamom, jaggery and a few almonds. It is a **vitamin B12 and calcium** treat that feels like a festival sweet.
steps: Drain the soaked rice and crush it lightly with the back of a spoon so it breaks and thickens the pudding.
Cook the rice in 150 ml of water over low heat, stirring now and then, until the water is mostly absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Add the soy beverage and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch, until soft and creamy.
Off the heat, stir in the jaggery, cardamom and almonds. It thickens as it cools, so loosen it with a splash of soy beverage if needed.
tip: Make it the night before if you like it thick: it sets to a spoonable pudding in the fridge and keeps a day.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Achari soya chunk bites
inspiredBy: North Indian achari tikka, with soya chunks in place of paneer or chicken
about: Soya chunks marinated in lemon, ginger, garlic and pickle-style spices (fennel, mustard seed and chili), then seared until charred at the edges. A high-protein snack with tikka-house flavour from a hot pan and **about 15 g of protein**.
steps: Boil the soya chunks in salted water for 8 minutes, drain and squeeze them dry.

Coarsely crush the fennel, mustard and fenugreek seeds, then toss the chunks with the oil, ginger, garlic, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, the crushed seeds, cumin, salt and half the lemon juice, and leave for 30 minutes.
Sear in a hot pan, turning, until browned and a little charred at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Squeeze over the rest of the lemon juice and eat hot.
tip: Boil and marinate the chunks the night before (or in the morning), and they sear in 8 minutes.

name: Soya tikki with mint chutney
inspiredBy: North Indian soya tikki
about: Golden shallow-fried patties of soy granules, besan, onion and green chili, with a sharp mint and cilantro chutney on the side. A snack with **nearly 20 g of protein** that tastes like a street-side tikki.
steps: Soak the soy granules in hot water for 10 minutes, then squeeze them very dry.

Pulse half the soaked granules with the besan and 2 tablespoons of water to a rough paste. Fold in the rest of the granules, the onion, half the cilantro, green chili, ginger, cumin, garam masala and salt, chill for 15 minutes, then shape into small patties with wet hands.
Shallow-fry the patties in the oil over medium heat until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes a side. Leave them untouched for the first 3 minutes so they hold together.
Blitz the mint, the rest of the cilantro and the lemon juice with a splash of water and a pinch of salt into a bright green chutney. Sprinkle the tikkis with chaat masala and serve with the chutney.
tip: Shape the patties the night before and keep them covered in the fridge, ready to fry. If the mix feels loose, add a spoonful more besan. Leave them alone in the pan for the first 3 minutes before you turn them.
ingredients: dry soy granules, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes and squeezed dry

name: Mushroom and soya chunk pepper fry
inspiredBy: Kerala pepper fry, usually made with beef, here with soya chunks and mushrooms
about: Oyster mushrooms and soya chunk strips fried dry with onion, curry leaves, lots of black pepper and crisp coconut slivers, in the style of a Kerala toddy-shop fry. It is hot, peppery and a bit addictive, with **about 12 g of protein** and plenty of B vitamins from the mushrooms.
steps: Boil the soya chunks in salted water for 8 minutes, drain, squeeze dry and tear into strips. Heat the oil in a pan and fry the coconut slivers until golden, about 1 minute. Scoop them out.
In the same oil, cook the onion with the curry leaves, garlic, ginger and green chili until the onion is deep golden, about 7 minutes.
Add the soya chunks and mushrooms with the turmeric, Kashmiri chili, pepper and salt, and fry over medium-high heat until the mushrooms have given up their water and the edges crisp, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the coconut and lemon juice and serve hot.
tip: Boil, squeeze and tear the soya chunks the night before and the fry takes 15 minutes.
ingredients: dry soya chunks, boiled 8 minutes, squeezed and torn into strips
oyster or white button mushrooms, torn into strips

name: Overnight oats with soy beverage, ground flax, walnuts and figs
inspiredBy: Greek and Levantine fig and walnut breakfasts, as an overnight jar
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in cinnamon soy beverage with chopped dried figs, ground flax and wheat germ, then topped with toasted walnuts for crunch. The figs melt into the oats and sweeten them, so you need no sugar. The fortified soy beverage brings **vitamin B12 and calcium**, and the flax and walnuts bring plant omega-3. Wheat germ adds **vitamin E and choline**.
steps: The night before, chop the figs and stir them into a jar with the oats, ground flax, wheat germ, cinnamon, salt and about ¾ cup of the soy beverage. It should look a little runny, since the oats, flax and wheat germ drink it up.
Cover and refrigerate overnight so the oats turn thick and creamy.
In the morning, give it a stir. It should be thick and spoonable, and a splash more soy beverage loosens it if it has gone stiff.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until you can smell them, then chop roughly.
Top the oats with the walnuts and drink the rest of the soy beverage alongside.
tip: Toast a week of walnuts on Sunday and keep them in a jar. Mix two oat jars at once, they keep for 3 days in the fridge.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton); about ¾ cup in the jar, the rest to drink alongside

name: Ful medames with lemon, tomato and parsley
inspiredBy: Egyptian ful medames and the Lebanese ful that mixes in a few chickpeas
about: Warm, garlicky fava beans and a few chickpeas mashed roughly with cumin and lemon, then topped with chopped tomato, onion and parsley and a good drizzle of olive oil, the way it is eaten in Cairo. You scoop it up with warm pita. The beans bring **iron and folate**, and the tomato and lemon help you absorb that iron.
steps: Mash the garlic with the salt into a paste. Warm the fava beans and chickpeas in a small pot with a splash of their liquid, the garlic and the cumin, stirring now and then, until steaming hot, about 5 minutes.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some whole beans for texture. Stir in the lemon juice and half the olive oil.
Spoon the beans into a shallow bowl. Drizzle with the rest of the olive oil, then pile on the tomato, onion and parsley and dust with Aleppo pepper.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the toaster and tear it up to scoop.
tip: A pinch of chili flakes or a few chopped pickles on top is very welcome.
ingredients: from a tin, with a little of the liquid

name: Chickpea fatteh with garlicky soy yogurt, tahini and toasted walnuts
inspiredBy: Lebanese and Syrian fattet hummus, with plain soy yogurt in place of the usual dairy yogurt
about: Warm chickpeas piled over crisp toasted pita, drenched in a cool, garlicky sauce of plain soy yogurt, tahini and lemon, and finished with sizzled walnuts, almonds and parsley. It is the traditional yogurt fatteh made plant-based, with hemp hearts blended into the sauce. The chickpeas and soy yogurt bring **protein and calcium**, the walnuts and hemp bring plant omega-3, and the glass of fortified soy beverage alongside adds **vitamin B12**.
steps: Tear the pita into bite-size pieces and toast them in a dry pan or a hot oven until golden and crisp, about 5 minutes.
Warm the chickpeas in a small pot with the cumin and a splash of water until steaming, about 5 minutes.
Mash the garlic with the salt, then blend or whisk it with the soy yogurt, tahini, hemp hearts and lemon juice until smooth. Thin with a spoonful of cold water if it is stiff.
Sizzle the walnuts and almonds in the olive oil for 1 to 2 minutes, until they smell toasty. Watch them, they scorch quickly.

Layer the pita in a bowl, spoon the chickpeas and a splash of the warm cooking water over it, pour on the yogurt sauce and finish with the hot nuts and oil, the parsley, sumac and Aleppo pepper. Warm the soy beverage with a pinch of cinnamon and drink it alongside.
tip: On a weekday, toast the pita and make the sauce the night before. In the morning it takes 10 minutes.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton), a glass, warmed, to drink alongside

name: Hummus bowl with roasted baharat tofu and seitan, cauliflower and tomato
inspiredBy: Lebanese hummus plates, with spiced roasted tofu and seitan where the meat would go
about: Thick, lemony hummus spread in a bowl and topped with crisp-edged tofu and seitan roasted with baharat, roasted cauliflower, a chopped cucumber and tomato salad and toasted almonds. Think of the hummus plates in Beirut, with tofu and seitan where the spiced meat would be. The calcium-set tofu and chickpeas bring **protein, iron and calcium**, and the cauliflower adds choline.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Pat the tofu dry, cut it and the seitan into cubes and toss with half the canola oil, the baharat and a pinch of salt. Toss the cauliflower florets with the rest of the canola oil and a pinch of salt. Roast both on a tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until the tofu and seitan edges are crisp and the cauliflower is browned.

Warm the chickpeas in a small pot with a splash of water for 3 minutes. Blend them with the tahini, half the lemon juice, the garlic, cumin and a few spoonfuls of ice water, in a mini processor if you have one, for a full 2 minutes until very smooth and creamy.
Chop the cucumber, tomato and parsley and toss with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Spread the hummus in a wide bowl, make a dip in the middle and drizzle in the olive oil.
Pile the tofu, seitan, cauliflower and salad on top, scatter over the almonds and dust with za'atar. Warm pita on the side is welcome.
tip: Monday's lunch is easiest made on Sunday: roast the tofu, seitan and cauliflower and blend the hummus, then pack them separately. A double batch of hummus blends smoother and keeps 4 days in the fridge.

name: Horiatiki with marinated tofu "feta" and white beans
inspiredBy: Greek horiatiki, as it is eaten on fasting days, with tofu in place of feta
about: A Greek village salad of ripe tomato, cucumber, pepper, olives and capers under a slab of lemony oregano tofu, with white beans and pita to make it a meal. It is the kind of thing Greek cooks put together on fasting days, when there is no cheese. The tofu brings **calcium and protein**, and the white beans bring iron and fibre.
steps: Press the tofu between towels for 10 minutes, then lay the slab in a shallow dish and spoon over half the lemon juice, half the vinegar, half the oregano and a good pinch of salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or leave it in the fridge in the morning or overnight.
Cut the tomato into wedges, the cucumber into thick half-moons and the pepper into rings, and slice the onion thinly.
Toss the vegetables with the white beans, olives, capers, the rest of the lemon juice and vinegar and most of the olive oil.
Spoon the salad onto a plate and set the tofu on top like a slab of feta. Drizzle with the last of the oil, the marinade and the rest of the oregano.
Toast the pita and tear it up to mop the juices.
tip: Marinate the tofu the night before or in the morning, it tastes much better after a few hours. Crumble it with your hands if you want it to look more like feta.
ingredients: pressed, cut in a thick slab

name: Mujaddara hamra with caramelized onions and lemony cabbage salad
inspiredBy: Lebanese mujaddara hamra, the bulgur version, with malfouf salad
about: Brown lentils and bulgur cooked together with cumin, topped with deep golden onions, and served with a crunchy lemon, garlic and mint cabbage and carrot salad. It is the Lebanese Lenten classic, plain food done properly. The lentils and bulgur together bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the lemony salad helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the lentils, cover with plenty of water and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until nearly tender but still holding their shape. Drain, saving the cooking water.

While the lentils simmer, slice the onions thin. Cook them in the canola oil over medium heat, stirring every few minutes and adding a splash of water if they catch, for 25 minutes, until deep golden and sweet. Take out a third and keep it for the top.
Stir the cumin and baharat into the onions left in the pot for 30 seconds, then add the bulgur, the lentils, the salt and enough of the lentil water to cover by about 2 cm.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Shred the cabbage finely and grate the carrot. Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt and toss it with the cabbage, carrot, lemon juice, olive oil and torn mint.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Serve the mujaddara topped with the reserved onions and the almonds, with the cabbage salad on the side. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Keep the cabbage salad in a separate container so it stays crunchy for tomorrow.

name: Gigantes plaki, giant white beans baked in tomato, dill and parsley
inspiredBy: Greek gigantes plaki, made with canned beans so it works on a weeknight
about: Creamy white beans baked in a sweet-sharp tomato sauce with celery, carrot, red pepper, chard and dill until the edges blister. It is Greek Lenten cooking at its best, and it tastes even better the next day. The beans bring **iron, calcium and fibre**, and a squeeze of lemon at the end helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C. Warm the olive oil in a wide ovenproof pan and cook the chopped onion, celery, pepper and diced carrot for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and oregano for 30 seconds, then add the crushed tomato, bay leaf, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Fold in the white beans, the chopped chard, half the dill and half the parsley, and slide the pan into the oven for 20 to 25 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the edges are browned.
Finish with the lemon juice and the rest of the herbs. Serve with crusty bread or warm pita if you like. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Cannellini work well here, and canned giant beans from a Greek grocer are even better. If you cook dried giant beans, soak them overnight and simmer them for about an hour before they go into the sauce.

name: Seitan, mushroom and cauliflower shawarma plate with garlic sauce and pickled carrot
inspiredBy: Lebanese shawarma, with seitan, mushrooms and cauliflower for the meat and a tofu garlic sauce for the toum
about: Baharat-spiced seitan, mushrooms and cauliflower roasted on one tray until the edges crisp, piled on a plate with a fluffy tofu garlic sauce, tomato, parsley and tangy pickled carrot, with warm pita on the side to scoop. It has the smoky, garlicky shawarma-stand flavour without the spit. The seitan and tofu together bring **protein, selenium and calcium**, and the vitamin D mushrooms add **vitamin D**.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 C. Cut the seitan into thin strips. Toss them with the baharat, paprika, cumin, half the lemon juice, half the garlic (mashed), half the canola oil and a good pinch of salt. Let them sit while the oven heats.
Meanwhile, toss the carrot ribbons with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and leave them to pickle.
Blend the tofu with the rest of the garlic, the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and a splash of cold water until fluffy and white, like toum.

Spread the seitan, mushrooms and cauliflower on one big tray (two if they crowd), drizzle the mushrooms and cauliflower with the rest of the oil, season them with a pinch of salt and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until browned and crisp at the edges.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the toaster.
Pile the seitan, mushrooms and cauliflower on a plate with the garlic sauce, tomato, parsley and the drained pickled carrot, and eat with the warm pita.
tip: Double the tofu garlic sauce, it keeps 4 days in the fridge and is good on the falafel too.
ingredients: sliced; sold as vitamin D mushrooms. Plain white mushrooms work, with less vitamin D

name: Baked chickpea and fava falafel in pita with roasted cauliflower and tahini sauce
inspiredBy: Lebanese and Egyptian falafel and ta'ameya, made with chickpeas and fava and baked instead of fried
about: Green, herby chickpea and fava falafel baked until crisp outside and fluffy inside, with warm pita, tahini sauce, a fresh tomato, cucumber and carrot salad and a side of roasted cauliflower. It has all the flavour of the street-stall version with a lot less oil. The chickpeas and fava beans bring **protein, iron and zinc**, and the cauliflower adds choline and vitamin C.
steps: The night before, cover the dried chickpeas and fava beans with plenty of cold water and soak for 12 hours. Drain well and, if you used whole fava beans, slip off the skins. Split, peeled fava beans skip this step.

Heat the oven to 220 C. Pulse the soaked chickpeas and fava beans (double the amount for two portions) in a food processor with the onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander and most of the salt until it looks like coarse couscous, not paste. Rest for 15 minutes so the beans bind.

Shape the mixture into 12 small patties (6 per portion). Toss the cauliflower florets with a third of the canola oil and a pinch of salt and spread them on a big tray. Put a second tray in the oven to preheat, then brush it with the remaining oil, set the falafel on it and brush the tops too.
Bake both trays for 25 minutes, turning the falafel once, until the falafel are deep golden and the cauliflower is browned at the edges.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce.

Dice the tomato and cucumber and toss with the grated carrot. Warm the pita, open it and tuck in a few falafel with some salad and tahini sauce. Eat the rest of the falafel, salad and cauliflower on the plate with the remaining sauce. Pack the second portion and the sauce for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: The beans must be soaked from dry. Canned ones turn to mush and the falafel fall apart. Leftover falafel are not good cold: reheat them for 8 minutes at 200 C and pack the tahini sauce separately.
ingredients: dried fava beans, peeled if you can find them, soaked overnight

name: Adas bi hamod, lemony lentil and chard soup with toasted pita
inspiredBy: Lebanese adas bi hamod, the lentil soup with chard and lemon
about: A thick Lebanese lentil soup with silky chard, garlic and plenty of lemon, topped with crisp toasted pita and a swirl of olive oil. It is bright, sour and deeply comforting, and a Lenten favourite. The lentils bring **protein, iron and folate**, and the chard adds vitamins A and K.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Warm the canola oil in a big pot and cook the chopped onion for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic, cumin and coriander and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils and plenty of water, enough to cover them by about 5 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft and falling apart.
Slice the chard stems thin and chop the leaves. Add the stems and cook for 5 minutes, then add the leaves for 3 minutes more, until silky.

Mash some of the soup against the side of the pot with a spoon, or give it a few pulses with a stick blender, so it is thick but still has texture. Add the salt and the lemon juice. It should taste distinctly sour.
Tear the pita into pieces and toast in a dry pan until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the pita, the parsley, a drizzle of the olive oil and a pinch of Aleppo pepper. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with the pita in a separate bag.
tip: Thin the leftovers with a splash of water when you reheat them. The soup thickens overnight.

name: Lenten chard and mushroom pie with tofu "feta"
inspiredBy: Greek hortopita and manitaropita, the Lenten (nistisimi) pies made with oil and no dairy
about: Crisp layers of oil-brushed phyllo around a lemony filling of chard, mushrooms, dill and herby crumbled tofu. It is the kind of fasting-season pie Greek families bake with no cheese or egg. The tofu brings **calcium and protein**, and the vitamin D mushrooms add **vitamin D** and niacin.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 C. Chop the chard, stems and all, and cook it in a dry pot over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until wilted. Tip it into a colander, cool for a few minutes, then squeeze out as much water as you can.

Cook the chopped onion and mushrooms in the olive oil for 8 minutes, until soft and the liquid has cooked off. Crumble the tofu into a big bowl with the lemon juice, oregano and most of the salt and let it stand while the chard drains.
Mix the chard, onion and mushrooms into the tofu with the dill, parsley, nutmeg, pepper and the rest of the salt. Taste, it should be bright and well seasoned.
Brush a baking dish with some of the canola oil. Lay in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each one lightly with oil, then spread the filling over.
Cover with the remaining phyllo, again brushing each sheet. Tuck in the edges, brush the top generously, and score the top layers into squares with a sharp knife.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Thaw frozen phyllo in the fridge overnight, so move the box from the freezer on Friday night. Keep the sheets under a damp towel while you work so they do not dry out and crack. Short on sheets? Skip the bottom layer and scrunch all the phyllo loosely over the filling, brushing as you go. Leftovers crisp up in a hot oven.
ingredients: finely chopped; sold as vitamin D mushrooms. Plain white mushrooms work, with less vitamin D

name: Sicilian caponata with white beans and chickpeas
inspiredBy: Sicilian caponata with a Levantine pomegranate molasses twist, served warm over white beans as a main
about: A sweet-sharp Sicilian eggplant stew with celery, olives, capers and toasted almonds, spooned warm over creamy white beans and chickpeas. It is Sicily's answer to ratatouille, with a bit of agrodolce bite. The beans and almonds bring **protein and calcium**, and the eggplant adds fibre.
steps: Toss the eggplant cubes with the canola oil and a pinch of salt, spread them on a tray and cover with foil. Roast at 220 C for 10 minutes, then take off the foil and roast 15 minutes more, until browned and soft. Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes and chop.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onion, celery and pepper for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the crushed tomato, olives and capers and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the roasted eggplant, the vinegar and the pomegranate molasses and simmer for 5 minutes, until glossy. It should taste sweet and sharp at once.
Warm the white beans and chickpeas in a small pot with a splash of water and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the beans into a bowl, top with the caponata and the almonds, and serve with toasted bread if you like.
tip: Caponata tastes even better made ahead. It keeps 4 days in the fridge, so you can cook it on Saturday and just warm the beans on Sunday.

name: Muhammara with cucumber sticks and pita
inspiredBy: Aleppo muhammara, the Syrian walnut and pepper dip
about: A smoky, tangy red pepper and walnut dip from Aleppo, with a hit of pomegranate molasses and Aleppo pepper, scooped up with cool cucumber and crisp pita. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**.
steps: Roast the pepper under a hot grill or over a flame for 10 to 15 minutes, turning, until the skin is blackened. Peel, seed and chop.
Toast the pita until dry and crisp, then break up half of it. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes. (Double the amounts for two portions.)
Blitz the pepper, walnuts, the broken pita, garlic, cumin, Aleppo pepper, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses and half the olive oil to a thick, rough paste. Season with the salt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the rest of the oil and serve with the cucumber sticks and the rest of the pita.
tip: This makes two portions, one for Monday and one for Thursday. Drained jarred roasted red peppers skip the first step.

name: Fig, flax and wheat germ shake with soy beverage
inspiredBy: the fig and date milk shakes of Egypt and the Levant
about: A thick, creamy shake of soft dried figs, fortified soy beverage, ground flax and wheat germ, spiced with cinnamon. Fig and date milk shakes are a classic cooler in Egypt and the Levant. A glass brings **vitamin B12, calcium and plant omega-3**, with vitamin E and selenium from the wheat germ.
steps: Soak the figs in a little hot water for 10 minutes if they are firm, then snip off the stems.
Blend the soy beverage, figs, ground flax, wheat germ and half the cinnamon until completely smooth, 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour into a tall glass and dust with the rest of the cinnamon.
ingredients: fortified with B12 and calcium (check the carton)

name: Lupini beans with lemon, mint and Aleppo pepper
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Levantine termis, the lupini bean snack
about: Plump, salty-sharp lupini beans, tossed with lemon, olive oil, fresh mint and a pinch of chili. They are a street snack from Cairo to Beirut. A bowl is one of the most **protein-rich** snacks you can eat.
steps: Drain the lupini and soak them in fresh cold water for 10 minutes to take the edge off the brine, then drain again.
Toss with the lemon juice, olive oil, torn mint and Aleppo pepper.
Serve with a lemon wedge. Squeeze each bean out of its skin with your teeth.
tip: Look for jarred lupini at Italian or Middle Eastern grocers, or at Costco.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and sumac
inspiredBy: warm green fava beans (ful akhdar) with lemon, as sold in spring across the Levant
about: Warm shelled green soybeans tossed with lemon, a pinch of sumac and a little salt, the way fresh green fava beans are eaten across the Levant in spring. A big bowl is a very **protein-rich** snack, with fibre and folate too.
steps: Simmer the frozen edamame in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, until tender, then drain well.
Toss with the lemon juice, olive oil and sumac while still warm.

name: Roasted peanuts with cumin and lemon
inspiredBy: the roasted peanuts sold from carts in Cairo and Beirut
about: Warm dry-roasted peanuts tossed with cumin, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of Aleppo pepper. Roasted peanuts are a favourite nibble all over the Levant and Egypt. The peanuts bring **protein, niacin and vitamin E**.
steps: Warm the peanuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Toss with the lemon juice, cumin and Aleppo pepper and eat warm.

name: Dried figs with toasted almonds
inspiredBy: the figs and nuts plate of Syria and Greece
about: Chewy, jammy dried figs with a handful of warm toasted almonds and a pinch of cinnamon. A figs-and-nuts plate is the simplest sweet in Syria and Greece. The almonds bring **vitamin E and calcium**, and the figs bring potassium and fibre.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Serve with the figs and a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Spiced seitan bites with lemon and parsley
inspiredBy: the crispy shawarma-pan bits of Lebanon, made with seitan
about: Little cubes of baharat-spiced seitan seared until crisp at the edges, tossed with lemon, parsley and a drizzle of tahini. Think of the crispy bits at the bottom of the shawarma pan. A serving brings **plenty of protein and selenium**.
steps: Cut the seitan into small cubes and toss with the baharat.
Sear in the canola oil over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until browned and crisp at the edges.
Toss with the lemon juice, parsley and a drizzle of tahini loosened with a spoonful of water.

name: Garlicky seitan tawook skewers with tomato
inspiredBy: Lebanese shish tawook, with seitan in place of chicken
about: Seitan cubes marinated in lemon, garlic and paprika, threaded on skewers and seared until golden, with a juicy tomato on the side. It is the shish tawook marinade on a plant-based protein. Seitan is a very **protein-dense** snack, and it brings selenium and niacin too.
steps: Cut the seitan into cubes and toss with the lemon juice, mashed garlic, paprika, salt and a spoonful of the canola oil. Leave for 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and sear in a hot pan with the rest of the oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Serve with the tomato cut in wedges and a scatter of parsley.

name: Seitan skewers with kafta spices, onion and parsley
inspiredBy: the flavours of Lebanese and Syrian kafta (grated onion, parsley and baharat) on seitan
about: Seitan cubes rubbed with grated onion, parsley and baharat, threaded on skewers and seared until golden. It has the flavours of the kafta grilled all over Lebanon and Syria. Seitan is a very **protein-dense** snack, with selenium and niacin too.
steps: Cut the seitan into bite-size cubes. Grate the onion and mix the pulp and juice with the chopped parsley, baharat and salt, then rub it all over the seitan and leave for 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers.
Sear in the canola oil over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and the onion catches at the edges. Squeeze over the lemon.

name: Hummus with carrot and cucumber sticks
inspiredBy: Lebanese hummus bil tahini, the everyday mezze
about: Creamy, lemony chickpea hummus with a swirl of olive oil, scooped up with crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks. It is the everyday mezze snack of Lebanon. The chickpeas and tahini bring **protein, iron and calcium**.
steps: Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and a few spoonfuls of cold water until very smooth.
Spoon into a bowl, make a dip in the middle and drizzle in the olive oil.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and serve alongside.

name: Roasted chickpeas with cumin and za'atar
inspiredBy: leblebi, the roasted chickpeas sold across the eastern Mediterranean
about: Crisp, crunchy chickpeas roasted with cumin and za'atar until they rattle. A snack bowl with the tangy, herby bite of za'atar. The chickpeas bring **protein and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Dry the chickpeas very well in a clean towel.
Toss with the canola oil, cumin and salt and roast for 25 minutes, shaking the tray twice, until crisp.
Toss with the za'atar while still warm.

name: Egg sauce with greens and pan-grilled ripe plantain
